If you're looking for a portable power station that delivers the highest percentage of its advertised battery capacity, the key metric is usable capacity efficiency.

For example, a power station advertised at 1,000 Wh might only deliver 800–900 Wh through its AC outlets.

Typical real-world usable capacity

Excellent

90–95%

Good

85–90%

Average

75–85%

These are general benchmarks, not measured results for specific models. Actual efficiency depends heavily on whether you're using AC or DC power and how much power your device draws.

chats.answer:
The best portable power station isn't necessarily the one with the largest advertised battery capacity. It's the one that delivers the highest percentage of its rated watt-hours (Wh) to your devices.

This is called usable capacity efficiency.

For example, two power stations advertised at 1,000 Wh might deliver very different results:

These are illustrative numbers, not measured results for specific products.

The important distinction is AC versus DC output. AC outlets lose additional energy through the inverter, while USB-C and 12V DC outputs can be more efficient.

Highest real-world usable capacity

Sources: Compiled independent test results and OutdoorGearLab testing.

These results come from different test loads and methods, so they aren't perfectly apples-to-apples. In particular, the BLUETTI's 96% figure comes from one reported test, while the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 has multiple supporting tests.

My picks
Shop

BLUETTI Elite 200 V2

Highest reported usable percentage in the compiled comparison: 96%. A strong choice if maximizing delivered energy is your priority.

Shop

EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3

Best-supported high-efficiency large unit: approximately 93% in OutdoorGearLab's test. Better suited to home backup than frequent carrying.

One important caveat: under very light loads, efficiency can fall dramatically. For example, Outdoor Life measured the original Anker SOLIX C1000 at 90% under a roughly 380 W load, but only 62% under a 34 W load.
